turns.title: The tagged firefly returns
turns.hypothesis: A callback should wake the session that spawned the run, not every desk in the same lab.
turns.attempt: A tiny robot releases a glowing callback firefly with a brass run tag while two sibling desks wait in the dark.
turns.result: Only the matching desk lights up. This illustrates run-ID-bound callback delivery without claiming the drawing is execution evidence.
turns.adaptation: Next, show why a clean exit is not enough without a receipt.
turns.story: The callback is a tagged firefly. It knows which desk asked for it.

turns.title: The bell is not the receipt
turns.hypothesis: A child can exit cleanly while still failing to prove that it completed the assigned task.
turns.attempt: The robot rings a tiny finished bell, but the outside verifier checks the receipt window before opening the gate.
turns.result: The gate stays shut because the receipt is blank. Terrarium would call this inconclusive instead of successful.
turns.adaptation: Next, show a parent launching several independent runs without becoming a swarm.
turns.story: Exit zero can make noise. A verified receipt opens the gate.

turns.title: Three pods, one explicit batch
turns.technique: Flat fan-out with a join condition
turns.hypothesis: Batch work should feel like one explicit parent planting independent runs, not a hidden swarm of agents.
turns.attempt: The parent robot plants three sealed seed pods. Each grows alone while the parent waits for the quorum marker to light up.
turns.result: Two pods bloom and the quorum is reached. The third pod can still be cancelled or inspected as its own run.
turns.adaptation: Next, show cancellation as a durable stop sign that survives the launch handoff.
turns.story: Batch fan-out is a gardener planting separate pods, not a swarm escaping the jar.

turns.title: The green seal has to be real
turns.hypothesis: A public story turn can follow a real receipt-hardening change without pretending the illustration is the proof.
turns.attempt: The robot offers the owl verifier a glowing green seal while empty scraps dissolve around the jar.
turns.result: Terrarium now rejects supplied verified-receipt summaries that are empty or non-string, while preserving legacy verified receipts that omit summaries.
turns.adaptation: Keep making the loop stricter about proof before storytelling.
turns.story: The owl does not accept blank magic. The seal has to glow with a real summary before the gate opens.

turns.title: Wrong model keys are not retry tickets
turns.hypothesis: A visible story beat can explain that some failures should be retried while bad runner configuration should be fixed.
turns.attempt: The robot tests a brass console; the owl marks the jammed key red while the green path stays reserved for retryable failures.
turns.result: Terrarium now classifies opencode model lookup/configuration failures as model-configuration with retryable false.
turns.adaptation: Keep making failures actionable before the loop asks another child to work.
turns.story: The owl does not hand out retry tickets for the wrong key. Some jams mean fix the console before sending another robot.
